title: Keema Aloo
subtitle: Spiced minced lamb with potato
excerpt: Minced lamb and diced potato cooked down with onion, tomato, and warm spices. A classic Anglo-Indian staple that is quick, filling, and budget friendly.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian home cooking tradition. Keema aloo is one of the most common weeknight curries in British-South Asian households.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight and reheat on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Keep a portion in the fridge for 3 days or freeze the rest.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead. The flavour deepens overnight. Reheat on the hob with a splash of water.

content.text: Keema aloo is minced lamb and potato cooked with onion, tomato, and spices. It gives a hearty, filling meal with very little fuss. Brown the mince well at the start or the curry will taste flat.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the lamb mince. Break it apart with a spoon and cook over a high heat for 6 minutes until browned.
Add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, and chilli powder. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes. Add the potato and salt. Stir well and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over a low heat for 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Remove the lid and cook for 3 more minutes to drive off any excess liquid.
Stir in the garam masala. Taste and adjust salt. Top with fresh coriander if using.

items.symptom: The mince is grey and soggy rather than brown.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough or the mince was added in a single lump.
items.fix: Use a high heat and break the mince into small pieces before adding. Give it space in the pan.

items.symptom: The potato is still firm after 20 minutes.
items.cause: The pieces were too large or the simmer was too gentle.
items.fix: Add a splash of water, replace the lid, and cook for another 10 minutes on a steady low simmer.

items.symptom: The curry is greasy on the surface.
items.cause: The lamb mince had a high fat content.
items.fix: Tilt the pan and spoon off the excess fat before adding the spices and tomatoes.
